newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil to begin work at North Sea Gungne field.
newsitem.headline: Statoil to begin work at North Sea Gungne field.

text.p: Hydrocarbon production at the Gungne field, south of Sleipner East in the North Sea, has been suspended since September 1, Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Thursday.
Output was halted after pressure in the well declined faster than expected, Statoil's Status Weekly newsletter said.
The company will begin an extensive workover of the well next week, which will take two to three weeks to complete.

Gungne, lying close to the Sleipner A platform, came on stream on April 21 and has produced two to three million cubic metres per day of gas and around 12,600 barrels per day of unstabilised condensate -- twice the expected flow, Statoil said.
Reserves are estimated at five million barrels of condensate, two billion cubic metres of gas and 265,000 tonnes of natural gas liquids.
"Faults or shale barriers in the structure mean we are not tapping the whole reservoir," said Bengt Rasmussen, drilling and well operations manager for Sleipner operations.
The Gungne well is 8,561 metres long with a horizontal offset of 7,377 metres.
